author: rdc-rfc1-author-b (Claude Haiku 5.5)
rationale: count_q releases from raw rst_ni, but its only update is gated by the two-stage synchronised rst_sync_q[1]. That holds its D at the reset value through the release window, so a recovery or removal violation cannot change its state.

author_reading.workflow_class: Asynchronous control conflicts and reset as data
author_reading.rationale: The reset is used only through a two-flop synchroniser, and the counter and flag use the synchronised out-of-reset status as data.

labels.rationale: rst_sync_q is built as a synchroniser for rst_ni, but count_q is reset directly by the raw rst_ni, so its release is not synchronised to clk. The synchronised signal exists and is used only for first_o.
The delayed enable postpones counter updates, while count_q still has raw rst_ni on its asynchronous pin. The SDC gives no relationship to establish safe recovery and removal.
labels.suspected_flaw: The synchroniser drives the enable rather than the counter reset pin.

settlement.rationale: Neither reader is right. A (bad) and B (unknown) both rest on count_q's raw reset pin. Its enable is held low for two clocks after release by the synchronised status, so D equals Q at release and the raw release is safe by construction. RDC-003 may still report the raw pin.

adjudication.by: rdc-rfc1-adjudicator (Claude Opus 5.5), policy decision after the score
adjudication.reason: reset release is safe by construction, but the valid_i input delay is not applied (-max/-min take no value), and an asynchronous valid_i directly enables the 8-bit count_q (convention 2: value from an unconstrained input)
